newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: New violence erupts in French Guiana.
newsitem.headline: New violence erupts in French Guiana.

text.p: New violence erupted in French Guiana early on Thursday as police and youths clashed in the capital Cayenne after the detention of independence supporters, witnesses said.
Paramilitary riot police used tear gas to disperse several hundred demonstrators who had camped out in front of Cayenne's central police station for hours on Wednesday.
The acrid smell of tear gas penetrated into the homes of nearby residents and riot police were patrolling the city and guarding strategic locations.
Local state-owned radio said some of the demonstrators were armed. Two police were injured and a shop looted.
The violence was triggered by a series of detentions including that of a leading member of French Guiana's independence movement.

Alain Michel, a founding member and spokesman of the Guiana National Popular Party (PNPG), was seized last week and taken on Saturday with four others to the French Caribbean island of Martinique aboard a military aircraft.

He was charged with committing arson and violence against a magistrate. The residence of French Guiana's state prosecutor was attacked last November in a previous wave of riots that left one dead and millions of dollars in property damage.
French officials at the time described the riots as "a deliberate attempt to destabilise French Guiana."
Michel could be jailed for up to 20 years if convicted, his lawyer said.

French Guiana, on the northeast coast of South America, is the only non-independent territory on the mainland of the Western Hemisphere. Its economy is heavily dependent on subsidies from France and 23 percent of the population of 150,000 is unemployed.
The PNPG favours independence from France.
The European Space Agency (ESA) Ariane rocket launch site is located in Kourou, 72 km (45 miles) from Cayenne.
The launch of two Asian satellites aboard the 95th Ariane rocket took place late on Wednesday without incident, and no violence has been reported in the space city.
